title: TrustGate: Significance Erosion and Guideline Exposure When Meta-Analyses Are Weighted by Trust
body: How many significant Cochrane meta-analytic findings survive when weighted by composite trust scores, and do low-trust meta-analyses disproportionately influence practice? We applied trust-weighted analysis to 888 significant meta-analyses from 6,229 Cochrane reviews, combining inverse-variance weighting adjusted by EvidenceScore with threshold gating at five levels and guideline exposure mapping across 14 domains. Trust-adjusted z-statistics were computed as the original z multiplied by the square root of the trust fraction, with results below 1.96 classified as eroded. At the B-plus threshold (score 70 or above), 63.9% of significant findings were eroded, with pain research most affected at 73.2% and cancer most resilient at 34.2% erosion. We identified 104 Red Flag meta-analyses combining low trust with high clinical influence across 12 reviews, alongside 366 Hidden Gems with high trust but low utilisation. Trust-calibrated synthesis could redirect clinical attention from unreliable toward underutilised high-quality meta-analyses. The influence score excludes direct guideline citation data, limiting precision of clinical exposure estimates.
